title: Choose the visual world for MrAnabolics
question: The roll assigned The Meet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Meet
options.lineage: sanctioned powerlifting competition - attempt cards, three-light judging, calibrated plates
options.thesis: A claim adjudicated in public. The meet is the one place this audience knows where you either made the lift or you did not, and three lights say so instantly - which is exactly what a purity claim has to do. Refuses the category near-black-plus-acid-green hype page AND the soft DTC wellness grid.
options.viewport: A live attempt board, not a hero image. Left: the featured compound set as an attempt card on white stock - lot number, class, and a row of three judge lamps resolving to white/white/white for tested, verified, in stock. Right: the loaded bar, where each calibrated plate is a category and its standardized color IS that category color for the rest of the site. Primary action sits where a judge signs.
options.risk: Sports signage slides into gym-bro loudness - the exact thing this redesign is escaping. The meet is bureaucratic and precise, not hype. If the condensed caps grow or a second red appears, it becomes a supplement ad.

raised.raise: Every product now shows its causal chain as one connected read - compound to concentration to half-life to protocol - instead of a flat spec dump.
State runs on one consistent channel with a visible trailing state (the lamps), never ad-hoc badge colors scattered per component.
Surfaces are built from the real materials of the system - card stock, plate color, chrome rule - never gradient-and-glass chrome standing in for a material.

options.label: The Monograph
options.lineage: printed pharmacopoeia - USP / Martindale drug reference
options.thesis: The catalog as a drug reference. Every compound is a monograph entry: ruled two-column text, structural formula, assay figures in monospace, thumb-index tabs down the edge for categories.
options.viewport: A single monograph spread - the featured compound entry, opened, with the index rail alongside it.
options.risk: This is where most careful runs in this category land: dense reference typography reads as serious almost automatically. It is the safe destination, and it under-serves the general-fitness half of the audience you asked me to split.

options.label: Night Instrument Panel
options.thesis: Six calm gauges, each owning one truth, read in a practiced cross-check sweep.
options.viewport: Products as gauge faces; deviation tilts the needle before any alarm fires.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright - trend-as-well-as-value is a genuinely better spec display than mine. Loses the other axis on your own brief: its native world is a matte black panel with a glowing green needle, which is both the category rut and the dark-only treatment you are rejecting.
options.risk: Rendered honestly it is a dark cockpit, and lightening it destroys the thing that makes it work.

options.label: The Rental Wall
options.lineage: friday-night video store, clamshells packed by genre
options.thesis: Browse sideways along spines; pull a box face-out to consider it; an empty slot with a tag is what out-of-stock looks like.
options.viewport: A full wall of spines by category, the featured product pulled face-out.
options.case: Holds clarity - present/absent as stock state and flip-to-read-spec is an excellent product-card model I would happily steal. Loses audience identification: video-store nostalgia is not native to anyone loading a bar, and the split audience would not see themselves in it.
options.risk: Reads as a themed novelty store rather than a place you trust with a purity claim.

options.label: Movida Scene Cover
options.thesis: Hard-cropped flash portrait, hand-inked masthead, cover lines thrown at angles in three fluorescent inks with no grid holding them.
options.viewport: The homepage as one cover: a cropped figure under a hand-drawn masthead, cover lines scattered over it.
options.case: Holds audience identification - the subcultural, slightly-underground energy genuinely rhymes with this scene. Loses product clarity decisively: no grid and angled cover lines destroy the specification tables that are the entire argument of this product.
options.risk: Everything legible about the catalog dies to make the cover work.

options.label: Fracture Glaze Shelf
options.case: Loses both. Lifters do not live in ceramics, and a world whose whole drama is uncontrolled variability argues the opposite of a purity claim.
options.kept: Cause and effect made visible per sample - recipe, thickness, position, final pool as one chain.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.case: Loses both. Near-black plus a glowing accent is precisely the treatment you asked me to remove, and attention-as-illumination hides the information this catalog has to show.
options.kept: One coherent state channel - attention, dormancy, bloom as luminance with afterglow.

options.label: Floated Pigment
options.case: Loses both. Marbling says nothing about dosage or purity, and its irreversible one-shot mark has no counterpart anywhere in a storefront.
options.kept: Every mark made by moving the real medium rather than drawing an imitation of it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean DTC wellness storefront, played straight and built impeccably: big product photography, generous white space, one accent, review stars, sticky add-to-cart.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor already expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every competitor by design - which is sometimes exactly what converts.
